I don't know why but the thought of engineering flight through a slow gradual process seems absolutely ridiculous to me, especially considering how many different kinds of animals supposedly individually evolved the ability.

Take two kids, Billy and Bobby. Billy is smaller than Bobby. They get food by jumping on animals from tree branches. Bobby is bigger and heavier and more likely to hurt himself falling. Eventually he seriously hurts himself and only Billy survives to pass on his genes. Survival of the fittest.

Billy has two kids, Johnny and Jack. They're about the same size, but Jack has crazy hair from some random mutation brought on by exposure to UV radiation or other genetic damage. The hair makes him float a bit when he leaps from the trees. This means he can jump further and makes him more maneuverable midair. All the bitches want Jack and his crazy hair. Jack has more offspring than Johnny. Survival of the fittest.

Over several generations you've got kids who are lighter and have better hair, who get more mates because they're better at jumping from trees. The kids that aren't good at jumping from trees injure themselves and remove themselves from the gene pool. The niche carved out by Billy and Jack and their offspring eventually deviate so far from their cousins that live in the grasslands who didn't have trees to climb that they look completely different. That's speciation and the survival of the fittest.
